## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Wèishēngyuàn jīng* (T507) is a one-fascicle short sūtra by [支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99) Zhī Qiān. The protagonist *Wèishēngyuàn* 未生冤 is a Chinese semantic translation of *Ajātaśatru* — "Foe-Yet-Unborn" — the famous king of Magadha who imprisoned his father Bimbisāra and converted to Buddhism after the Buddha's death. This is one of the earliest Chinese sūtras specifically about Ajātaśatru.

**Abstract**

The Ajātaśatru narrative is one of the most important historical-mythical episodes in the Buddhist canon, treated extensively in the Pāli *Sāmaññaphala-sutta* and many Mahāyāna sources. Zhī Qiān's translation is dated to his Wú productive period (222–252 CE).
